To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bacteriocin activity of LAB strains was affected by culture media, pH, and temperature.
the bacteriocin production and growth of the LAB were significantly affected by culture media, initial pH of the culture media and incubation temperatures.
growth and bacteriocinin production of bacteriocineogenic LAB was affected by culture media, pH, and growth temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of culture media, initial pH and temperature on bacteriocin production.
understanding the influence of growth conditions on LAB growth and bacteriosin production, which will provide useful information for future application of LAB in food industry.
the optimization of bacteriocin production from LAB and the development of new bacteriocins as potential food biopreservation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bacteriocinogenic strains of L. curvatus, E. faecium, and L. paracasei sub sp. paracase are suitable for use in the fermentation of foods.
the bacteriocin activity is significantly affected by the culture media and initial pH.
the bacteriocin production was influenced by the type of media, pH, temperature and the type of strain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bacteriocins production was affected by growth conditions and the optimal conditions to produce bacteriocinogenic activity were found at pH 6.5 and 37 °C in MRS broth.
LAB growth was significantly influenced by initial pH of culture medium (p <0.001) with optimal pH ranging from 6 to 7.
the optimal condition for the growth of bacteriocin-producing LAB was found in MRS broth at pH 6.5 and temperature 37 °C.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth conditions of bacteriocin-producing LAB are important factors that should be considered in the food industry.

the optimal growth conditions are important for both LAB growth as well as bacteriocin production and the results from this study could be useful for further studies on the use of bacteriocin as natural preservatives.
the optimal conditions for growth and bacteriocines production of bacteriocins LAB are not always the same.
